newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse starts week with falling prices.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse starts week with falling prices.

text.p: Leading Hungarian issues descended in slack trading on Monday as not only the Russian president's health but also expectations of a U.S. rate hike urged investors to scale down their activities, traders said.
The BUX index of the Budapest Stock Exchange ended at 3,512.86 points, down 37.34. Spot share turnover totalled a maigre 561.2 million forints.
"Expectations of a U.S. rate increase are the main reason for today's low activity," said Adam Santha of Daiwa-MKB Rt.
The U.S Federal Open Market Committee will meet on Tuesday.
"Also, the drop of yields stopped and yields now rise," Santha said, referring to last week's T-bill yield movements.
Traders said that Boris Yeltsin's health was also a key question, but Santha saw its impact more indirect.
On Monday a few shares, including Inter-Europa Bank and Soproni brewery, bucked the bearish trend and rose.
Nevertheless, traders did not see any particular reasons behind the price increases as they traded in thin volumes as the corporate side is calm these days.
Inter-Europa Bank firmed over six percent or 2,200 forints to end at 37,250, while Soproni brewery put on 320 forints to close at 2,320.
